claims.claim: A Purview Data Map scan of a same-tenant Fabric tenant supports full, incremental and scoped scans and brings in metadata and lineage. For items other than Power BI, only item-level metadata and lineage, with sub-item metadata for lakehouse tables and files. Once metadata is in Purview, Purview permissions, not Fabric permissions, decide who sees it.
The Data Map source table lists Fabric with no automatic classification and no sensitivity labels applied to Data Map assets, with lineage and live view supported.

The OneLake catalog Govern section reports sensitivity label coverage and unlabelled items, refreshes from admin monitoring storage once a day, and does not include subitems such as tables. It is rolling out by region, with no preview label on the page.

Fabric activities are in the Microsoft Purview audit log; searching it needs the Audit Logs role. Audit (Standard) retains 180 days; Audit (Premium) up to one year by policy and ten years with an add-on licence; Search-UnifiedAuditLog and CSV export are available.

concept_html:
An auditor asks three questions about talent data. What do you hold? How is it protected? Who touched it? Answer each with evidence from a system, dated, not with a statement of intent. Fabric and Purview give you one source for each.

What you hold: a Purview Data Map scan. Register the Fabric tenant in the Microsoft Purview Data Map and scan it, in full, incrementally, or scoped to chosen workspaces. The scan brings in item metadata and lineage. For lakehouses it also reads tables and files. Two limits matter. The scan does not classify or label Fabric data. And once metadata reaches Purview, Purview permissions, not Fabric roles, decide who sees it, so restrict the collection that holds HR items.

How it is protected: label coverage. The Govern tab of the OneLake catalog reports the share of items with no sensitivity label, by workspace and item type. It refreshes once a day, and it does not count tables inside an item.

Who touched it: the audit log. Fabric records activities in the Microsoft Purview unified audit log. You need the Audit Logs role to search it. Export results to CSV, or script the search with Search-UnifiedAuditLog. Audit (Standard) keeps records for 180 days. Audit (Premium) keeps them up to a year by policy, longer with an add-on licence.

If your audit period is longer than your retention, export on a schedule into storage you control.

An evidence pack holds the scan date and scope, label coverage per workspace with the gaps listed, and the access records for sensitive items, each with the query that produced it. Status: the scan and the audit log are generally available. The Govern tab has no preview label but is still rolling out by region (Microsoft Learn, November 2026).

exercises.primer:
`dict.setdefault(key, default)` returns the value for `key`, adding `default` first if the key is missing:

```python
counts = {}
counts.setdefault("red", [0, 0])[0] += 1
counts   # {"red": [1, 0]}
```

`"key" in some_dict` checks whether a key exists: `"a" in {"a": 1}` is `True`.

Write `label_coverage(items: list[dict]) -> dict[str, float]`. Each item is a dict with `"workspace"` and `"label"`, where `"label"` is a label name or `None`.

Return, for each workspace that has items, the share of its items with a label, from 0.0 to 1.0. Return an empty dict for an empty list. Raise `ValueError` if an item has no `"workspace"` key.

solution_lines: def label_coverage(items: list[dict]) -> dict[str, float]:
"""Share of items with a sensitivity label, per workspace.
items: Dicts with "workspace" and "label", where label is a name or None.
Workspace to the share of its items that carry a label, from 0.0 to 1.0.
ValueError: If an item has no "workspace" key.
counts: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
if "workspace" not in item:
raise ValueError(f"item without a workspace: {item}")
tally = counts.setdefault(item["workspace"], [0, 0])
tally[1] += 1
if item.get("label") is not None:
tally[0] += 1
return {workspace: labelled / total for workspace, (labelled, total) in counts.items()}

title: Audit evidence, Purview scans, label coverage and the audit log
why_html: An internal audit asked who had opened the salary semantic model in the last financial year. The team ran an audit search in month 11. Audit (Standard) returned only the last six months, because the first five had expired. The finding read "access cannot be evidenced for 5 of 12 months". A monthly export would have closed it.
